change: Resolve chains of reviewed gate replacements across revisions, retire unused work classifications and distinguish available delivery from cancelled work.
evolution.data_plan: Exercise versioned synthetic repositories. Product persistence and wire formats are unchanged.
evolution.cleanup: Reuse the existing task graph, gate records and check commands. Restore focus to M1-006 after evidence is recorded.

tasks.title: Run development in Herdr and bind model use to local user content boundaries
acceptance: A developer can launch a bounded task in Herdr using the requested implementation or supervision model. Parallel writers have explicit ownership, one integrator and verified results. Ordinary changes and necessary tooling installation proceed under the existing owner grant.

Local conversations, memory, strategies and their derived data have accountable storage, recovery and downstream-use requirements. Activating a model grants ordinary in-session use within the disclosed scope. Sharing saved private content uses only the selected preview for the named destination.

Automated qualification distinguishes ordinary chat from private excerpt transfer, and retained verification artifacts exclude unrelated personal files. Product implementation and real model acceptance stay attributable to the product tasks.

plan.outcome: A new development session can start its own Herdr implementation and review work while protecting local product records and keeping ordinary connected-model turns usable.
hypotheses: The installed Herdr core can run the actual repository and both requested Codex model profiles without changing account defaults. Existing evidence collection and model authorization need a distinction between routine requests and saved private content.

risks.failure: A helper changes someone else’s work or a launcher silently substitutes the wrong model.
A cloud route receives saved history or the evidence upload includes a private record.

plan.rollback: Keep the existing local checks and prior delivery evidence. Retain any failed isolated fixture, revert the affected tooling change, and leave product runtime connections disabled until qualified.

non_goals: Implementing a complete storage engine, provisioning a paid product model, or exporting real product content in scaffold tests.

preserve: A fresh offline chart, specific third-party source rights, provider choice and existing local verification commands.
change: Adopt Herdr for active development and one-time cloud connection scope with separate approval for selected saved private excerpts.
evolution.data_plan: Use repository code and synthetic fixtures for all development, subprocess and hosted verification. Keep owned product records and backups in local application storage.
evolution.cleanup: Reuse the task ledger and native Herdr terminals. Inspect delivered changes, retire only owned temporary sessions and restore the product focus.

tasks.title: Correct synthetic market freshness and read explicit quality revisions
acceptance: Derive freshness from the declared observation schedule, cutoff and source delay independently of known gaps or loss of connection. A scheduled close, old historical date or missing evidence alone never implies stale. Preserve existing normal snapshot hashes and normal legacy metadata semantics.

Read the known explicit stale and gapped fixture revisions through the existing versioned history request, retain exact series and snapshot identity, and reject unknown revisions. A known stale series with a gap preserves both facts under the legacy gapped summary.

plan.outcome: Consumers of a frozen history page can distinguish coverage and freshness and explicitly replay the supplied sample revision through the existing operation.
hypotheses: A typed expectation for the synthetic sample and a bounded mapping to its revisions suffice without a new operation or provider. The data change can be completed independently of the replay UI.

risks.failure: A gap hides a missed update or missing evidence invents an open or stale state.
A pinned sample silently resolves to different bars or a normal snapshot changes.

plan.rollback: Retain failed vectors and revert the affected sample selector or derivation. No user files or stored data need migration.

non_goals: Real market access, UI presentation, native process lifetime and subscription transport.

preserve: Normal 1.0 and 1.1 synthetic history, stable frozen bar digests and explicit sample opt-in.
change: Derive independent freshness and coverage and honor recognized explicitly pinned quality revisions.
evolution.data_plan: Existing frozen normal inputs keep their identities. Only checked-in synthetic data is involved.
evolution.cleanup: Use a single quality derivation and remove reliance on a legacy display label as input.

tasks.title: Preserve failure diagnostics on Windows consoles
acceptance: A failed check containing Unicode outside the console encoding retains its diagnostic log and returns the original failed check result so the run can finalize and stage evidence. Receipt hashes still bind the original bytes.

plan.outcome: A check failure is diagnosable from the finalized run even on a legacy Windows console.
hypotheses: The failure occurs only when the diagnostic tail is printed. Keeping raw bytes in the log and encoding a short console result safely preserves both diagnostics and the failed gate.

risks.failure: Reporting raises a second exception and hides the original failure, or a private stdout is printed.

plan.rollback: Retain the hosted console and local recovery snapshot. Run the affected check with its isolated log while repairing the harness, then rerun native verification.

non_goals: Mask the failed product check, change the process timeout or claim physical Windows acceptance.

preserve: Original raw check-log bytes, digest, exit code and redacted private check output.
change: Console diagnostics remain parseable even when their text includes characters outside its code page.
evolution.data_plan: No stored product data changes. Existing reports stay readable.
evolution.cleanup: Use the existing structured harness output and keep a single private-log policy.

tasks.title: Align shared-selection and durable mutation revision requirements
acceptance: The product rule, human request and AI tool intent agree on the independent selection and durable workspace revision preconditions. Shared vectors reject substitution of either revision for the other and preserve valid 1.1 callers.

plan.outcome: A developer implementing shared selection or a selection-bound durable write can identify the right revision without changing protocol 1.1 payloads.
hypotheses: The wire structs already encode both forms of optimistic concurrency. The broad AI policy sentence disagrees with the specific selection contract.

risks.failure: Requiring a workspace revision for selection rejects valid clients, or substituting a selection token for the durable revision allows a stale mutation.

plan.rollback: Retain the accepted 1.1 schemas and regression vectors. Revisit the policy and add a versioned change only if existing callers actually require a different wire shape.

non_goals: Implement durable storage, authorize a new actor, change wire identifiers or mark any planned workspace operation implemented.

preserve: Wire 1.1 human and AI requests, current grant checks, and independent selection tokens.
change: Make the revision requirement for each operation explicit and exercise wrong-token substitution.
evolution.data_plan: No saved or transmitted data format changes.
evolution.cleanup: Replace the conflicting blanket instruction with the rules already used by the registered commands.

tasks.title: Clarify committed replay and shared evidence target forms
acceptance: New operations revalidate the current target revisions and required confirmation. An already committed semantic retry recovers only its permitted receipt through the existing scoped replay rules. Both human and AI requests can select an identified workspace object or explicitly clear selection, and omission of the target is rejected.

plan.outcome: A caller can recover a lost committed response after its revisions advance and can select or explicitly clear any supported evidence target under its current grant.
hypotheses: The 1.1 target union already supports workspace objects and null. The established replay authorization applies before evaluating new-work revision and confirmation preconditions.

risks.failure: A retry is rejected just because the original commit advanced a revision, or it discloses the earlier result after access was revoked.
One caller rejects a workspace object or accepts an omitted target as an explicit clear.

plan.rollback: Retain the accepted 1.1 schema, receipts and examples. Fix only the normative cross-references and examples if an implementation precondition conflicts.

non_goals: Implement durable operations, generalize grants, or publish a release. Runtime transaction ordering is an M2-001 acceptance case.

preserve: The 1.1 target union, scoped idempotency key and current disclosure rules.
change: Describe committed-retry ordering, all shared target families and explicit clearing consistently.
evolution.data_plan: No stored data or wire format changes.
evolution.cleanup: Remove ambiguous new-work wording from the receipt recovery and object-selection paths.
